summary: A 1924 log cupola cabin at a 1922 detection camp was replaced in 1954 by the current L-4 tower, now on emergency-use status overlooking Hells Canyon.

facts.design: 1936-model L-4 cab, 41-foot timber tower with catwalk
facts.status_note: On emergency-use status rather than staffed every season.

access.note: Easy drive-up access reported by visitors, but not a public rental; emergency-use Forest Service lookout.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Nez Perce National Forest)

events.note: Fire detection camp first established at the site.
Current 41-foot timber tower with 1936-model L-4 cab and catwalk built, replacing the 1924 cupola cabin.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, April 24, 2009, as US 788.

evidence.supports: 1954 tower replaced 1924 log cupola cabin; falcon hacking use; location overlooking Salmon River and Hells Canyon.
evidence.quote: The 41' timber tower with a 1936-model L-4 cab with catwalk was built in 1954, replacing a log cupola cabin built in 1924... The lookout was used as a site for hacking falcons for several years.

evidence.supports: NHLR registration date and registry number.

evidence.quote: Started as a camp in 1922, a log cupola cabin was built in 1924. This was replaced by the present 41' treated timber L-4 tower in 1954.

evidence.supports: Current emergency-use status, sturdy condition, rental-program suggestion, and visitor description of condition and access.
evidence.quote: The lookout is in sturdy shape and to our eyes we thought it would make a great addition to the rental program with just a little bit of TLC. This tower is currently on Emergency Use status. This is a great tower to visit with easy drive up access and a truly spectacular western view overlooking the Hells Canyon area.

notes_for_editor: The brief listed status as plain 'standing'; sources indicate it's specifically on emergency-use status rather than seasonally staffed, so I added status_note and staffing accordingly. Idaho Fire Lookouts visit post includes several Fire Lookout Museum photos already credited there; not treated as new finds here since they're attributed to that site rather than a fresh source.
